topic: Design Critique, Heuristic Evaluation, and UX Improvement
learningObjectives: Apply usability heuristics to evaluate interface designs.
Identify usability problems and explain their underlying causes.
Propose evidence-based improvements to interface experiences.

activities.title: Heuristic Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the key principles used in heuristic evaluation.

content.concept: Heuristic evaluation uses established usability principles to identify potential interface problems systematically.
content.tip: Select each heuristic to see the type of problem it helps identify.

items.label: Visibility of System Status
items.description: Keep users informed about what the system is doing.

items.label: Match Between System and Real World
items.description: Use language and concepts familiar to users.

items.label: User Control and Freedom
items.description: Provide ways to undo, cancel, or recover from actions.

items.label: Consistency and Standards
items.description: Use familiar patterns and consistent terminology.

items.label: Error Prevention
items.description: Prevent mistakes before they happen whenever possible.

items.label: Recognition Rather Than Recall
items.description: Make options and information visible so users do not have to remember them.

activities.title: Heuristic Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each interface problem to the heuristic it violates.

content.concept: Common usability principles address visibility, consistency, error prevention, user control, recognition, and simplicity.
content.tip: Focus on the underlying usability problem rather than the visual appearance.

pairs.prompt: The system gives no indication that a file upload is still processing.
The same action is labeled 'Save' on one page and 'Store' on another.
A destructive action occurs immediately with no cancel or undo option.
The form accepts invalid data and reports the problem only after submission.
Users must remember a product code from a previous screen.

activities.title: Design Critique Lab
activities.instruction: Identify the primary usability issue and explain why it affects the user.

content.concept: A useful critique describes the observed problem, its user impact, and a possible improvement rather than focusing only on personal preference.
content.tip: Base your critique on observable behavior and user impact.

scenarios.question: A checkout page has three buttons: 'Continue', 'Proceed', and 'Next', all leading to different actions.
scenarios.explanation: Similar labels for different actions make it harder to predict outcomes.

scenarios.question: A loading screen provides no indication of progress during a long upload.
scenarios.explanation: Users need feedback about ongoing operations.

scenarios.question: A delete button appears next to a save button with no confirmation.
scenarios.explanation: Destructive actions should reduce the chance of accidental activation.

activities.title: Improvement Builder
activities.instruction: Assemble an improvement that directly addresses the identified usability issue.

content.concept: Design improvements should connect directly to observed user problems and preserve important user goals and constraints.
content.tip: Choose improvements that solve the actual problem rather than adding unrelated visual changes.
